title: The child who did not wake

plan.english: Little son, why did you not wake? In the evening you drank milk from my breast. Then at dawn you were cold. Hunger took you, and it did not take me. I weep indeed, and your father weeps. Now lie, my son, in the earth.

plan.english: Long was the winter, and long was the hunger. Then the nights were cold. The grain vanished, and the cows died in the stalls. We devoured the bark of the trees, we ate the dogs. The old men went out into the snow, they did not come back. Who will praise the old men? We, the living, shall praise them.

clauses.english: Long was the winter, and long was the hunger.

We devoured the bark of the trees, we ate the dogs.
The old men went out into the snow, they did not come back.
Who will praise the old men?
We, the living, shall praise them.

plan.english: Then the plague came into our house, and it took my husband. It took my daughter too. I am a widow, and I sit at the hearth. No one speaks inside the house. Gods, why then did you take them and leave me?

plan.english: Good cows, you lie in the field. Cows, I milked you in the morning. The evil sickness came in the evening. In the night you were dead. My herd is gone, the children are hungry. What will the children eat in the winter?

plan.english: In that winter the snow fell early. The herds did not find grass, and the cows died in the stalls. Then the people ate their flesh. The grain vanished from the pots. Then hunger arrived in the village. The children wept in the nights, and the mothers gave them nothing. Then the spring came, and few sheep were alive.

The grain vanished from the pots.
Then hunger arrived in the village.
The children wept in the nights, and the mothers gave them nothing.
Then the spring came, and few sheep were alive.

title: The old woman and the cold

plan.english: There was an old woman in a village. In the hunger she spoke to her son. Lead me out into the cold, son. I eat, and I do not work. The son wept, and he led her out in the night. She sat down under a tree, and she did not speak. In the morning the son came back. The old woman was cold, and she did not breathe. But the children of the son lived.

clauses.english: There was an old woman in a village.
In the hunger she spoke to her son.
Lead me out into the cold, son.
I eat, and I do not work.
The son wept, and he led her out in the night.
She sat down under a tree, and she did not speak.
In the morning the son came back.
The old woman was cold, and she did not breathe.
But the children of the son lived.

plan.english: The villagers waited for the spring. The snow lay on the fields, and the ice lay on the river. The cows died. Then the dogs died. A young herdsman went to the hills, and he was seeking roots. He did not come back. Then the sun became warm, and the snow was melting. The grass grew, and no one ate it. The spring came, and few people were alive.

clauses.english: The villagers waited for the spring.
The snow lay on the fields, and the ice lay on the river.
The cows died.
Then the dogs died.
A young herdsman went to the hills, and he was seeking roots.
He did not come back.
Then the sun became warm, and the snow was melting.
The grass grew, and no one ate it.
The spring came, and few people were alive.

plan.english: A stranger came to the village in the evening. The villagers gave him food and a bed. At dawn he went away. But the plague remained in that house. The children were coughing. Then the mother burned with heat. From that house it went into the houses. Many died, and the living fled to the hills. Now the villagers fear strangers.

clauses.english: A stranger came to the village in the evening.
The villagers gave him food and a bed.
At dawn he went away.
But the plague remained in that house.
The children were coughing.
Then the mother burned with heat.
From that house it went into the houses.
Many died, and the living fled to the hills.
Now the villagers fear strangers.

plan.english: A shepherd had a hundred sheep. In one winter a sickness came to them. They coughed, and they lay down, and they did not stand up. The shepherd burned the dead ones in a great fire. Ten sheep lived. He drove them to the mountain. In the spring there were lambs. The shepherd praised the gods.

clauses.english: A shepherd had a hundred sheep.
In one winter a sickness came to them.
They coughed, and they lay down, and they did not stand up.
The shepherd burned the dead ones in a great fire.
Ten sheep lived.
He drove them to the mountain.
In the spring there were lambs.
The shepherd praised the gods.

title: The wise woman and the worm

plan.english: A child lay in sickness, and his belly was swelling. His mother brought a wise old woman. She looked at the child, and she spoke. A worm is devouring him inside. For nine nights she chanted the song. Then the worm came out of the mouth of the child. She ground it with a stone, and she threw it into the fire. The child woke up and ate. The mother gave the old woman a cow.

plan.english: In one summer it did not rain. The rivers dried up, and the grass became dry. The cattle stood at the spring, and they did not find water. The king led the villagers to the assembly. They took counsel. Let us give the greatest bull to Perkʷunos. They slew the bull on the stone, and the smoke went up to the sky. Then Perkʷunos thundered, and it rained. The villagers wept with joy.

plan.english: In the hunger the elders were sitting in the assembly. One said: May the warriors eat, and they will guard the village. Another said: May the children eat. They are our offspring. The oldest woman stood up, and she spoke. We old ones have eaten for many years. May the young ones eat. The elders were silent, and they did so.
